why: Each blend case sets D3DRS_SRCBLEND (19), pushes its own D3DRS_DESTBLEND (20) value and jumps to a SetRenderState shared by cases with different values. Hex-Rays made the pushed value a fourth argument (v35, never assigned) of the first call, dropped it from the shared one, and merged case 73 (DESTBLEND 2) with cases 3 and 68 (DESTBLEND 6). Separately, IDA's stack pointer is one dword off from the jump-only block 0x10046E6E to the D3DRS_ZFUNC call: Hex-Rays gave SetRenderState(137, 0) a third argument (v2, the never-assigned EDI) and took the pushed 4 from SetRenderState(D3DRS_ZFUNC, 4).
evidence: jump table 0x10047234 indexed by bytes at 0x1004725C. 0x10046886 (case 0): 19,2 then push 1 -> 0x100469A0 (20). 0x100468A5 (73): 19,5, push 2. 0x10046986 (3, 68): push 5 -> 0x10046988 (19), push 6. 0x100468C4 (70, 71): push 1 -> 0x10046988, push 6. 0x100468CB (100): 19,5, push 6 -> 0x10046901 (20, then the byte at 0x1047BC0F). 0x100468E7 (104): 19,5, push 2 -> 0x10046901. 0x1004694F (72): 19,5; 20,2; flag 1. 0x10046E73: push 0; push 0x89; push dev; call [edx+0xC8] (two arguments, like the other branch at 0x10046E56). 0x10046F7F: push 4; push 0x17; push dev; call [ecx+0xC8].
